title: Pickled Part Three (The Rematch)
style: 1920s australian vaudeville banjo, 150 BPM, plucked banjo lead, kazoo fanfare, washboard percussion, ukulele strum, jaunty upright bass, two male vocals trading lines with broad aussie accents, comedic redemption arc turning to acceptance, music hall energy, happy bouncing tempo
lyrics:
[Intro — banjo flourish, kazoo fanfare, washboard scrape]
We've come back, mate! New paddles, fresh socks!
This time we're winnin' — on the rocks!

[Verse 1 — both, alternating, confident]
[mate] We trained for a fortnight, we drilled every shot
[partner] We watched all the YouTubes, we ate not a lot
[mate] No meat pies at point seven this time round
[partner] Eyes on the ball, feet on the ground!

[Pre-Chorus — both, building]
We're the comeback kings of the Tuesday court
We've come for the granny in the knee-brace short
Last week we got pickled, eleven to nowt
This week we are gonna sort it out!

[Chorus — both, anthem]
Pickled Part Three! Pickled Part Three!
The rematch round of the century!
Same court, same lady, same kazoo crowd
But this time we're playin' loud and PROUD!
Redemption Tuesday — here we come!

[Verse 2 — confidence cracking]
[mate] Score's at one-nil, we're in control
[partner] Two-nil! Three-nil! We're on a roll!
[mate] …four-nil to them now, what just happened, mate?
[partner] She did the soft scoop, I was waltzin' too late!

[Pre-Chorus — panic creeping in]
Brain's startin' to wander, eyes on the snack van
Sausage roll callin' from the shire-hall caravan
Feet are still movin', but the noggin' is gone
The granny is hummin' Waltzing Matilda again!

[Chorus — both, deflating]
Pickled Part Three! Pickled Part Three!
The rematch round of the century!
Same court, same lady, same kazoo crowd
And this time we're losin' even MORE loud!
Redemption Tuesday — there it goes!

[Bridge — banjo solo, then spoken truce with the granny]
[granny, kindly] Boys… have a sit down.
[mate, panting] Yes ma'am.
[partner, panting] Yes ma'am.
[granny] You played a lot better.
[mate] We did?
[granny] No. But the scoreline was closer.
[partner] How close?
[granny] Eleven to two, instead of eleven to nowt.
[both, defeated] CRIKEY.

[Verse 3 — acceptance]
[mate] Maybe pickleball isn't about winnin' at all
[partner] Maybe it's about gettin' beat by a granny in fall
[mate] She's eighty-three with a plywood paddle
[partner] And we're forty-five with our brains in a saddle
[both] Saddle, saddle, brain in a saddle!

[Final Chorus — full banjo cranked, washboard mad, kazoo blowin']
Pickled Part Three! Pickled Part Three!
We came for revenge and we got cherry tea!
Same court, same lady, same kazoo crowd
She pickled us proudly, we lost extra loud!
Redemption Tuesday — call it Tuesday Three!

[Outro — banjo wind-down, kazoo huff, spoken peace]
[granny] Same time next Tuesday, boys?
[mate] Yes ma'am.
[partner] Bring extra pies.
[granny] I'll bring the cucumber sandwiches.
[both] CRIKEY!
[banjo flourish, kazoo whoop, washboard scrape]
